name: Stummerberg
kurzbeschreibung: Sunny mountain village above Stumm, featuring traditional farms and stunning panoramic views.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Stummerberg stretches across sun-drenched mountain pastures overlooking the central Zillertal in the district of Schwaz. Situated at an average altitude of approximately 800 meters above sea level – with settlements extending from 560 meters to over 1,250 meters – this mountain community presents an expansive sanctuary of alpine tranquility. With around 876 residents and a territory covering 56.7 square kilometers, Stummerberg is the third-largest municipality by area in the Zillertal, largely encompassing the vast, untouched high valley of the Märzengrund. The rural community comprises three distinct hamlets: Stummerberg, Kleinstummerberg, and Gattererberg. From flower-bedecked timber balconies of historic farms, breathtaking panoramic views unfold over the entire Zillertal and the rugged peaks of the Tux Alps.

Geschichte

Archaeological discoveries, such as a Bronze Age axe head found near the Klammlhof, attest to human presence on these sunny terraces millennia ago. During the High Middle Ages, these steep slopes were cleared and settled as pastoral dairy farms (Schwaighöfe) under the ownership of Herrenchiemsee Abbey and the Archbishopric of Salzburg, with farmers paying tithes in lard, alpine cheese, and livestock. The first official documentation dates to 1143, when Salzburg Archbishop Konrad transferred an estate on the mons supra Stume (mountain above Stumm) to Herrenchiemsee. For generations, the mountain dwellings remained subject to the jurisdiction of the Hofmark Stumm. In 1849, during regional municipal reforms, the communities of Stummerberg and Gattererberg united to form an autonomous municipality. To this day, vibrant alpine farming traditions shape everyday life, entirely removed from bustling commercial tourism.

Anreise

Reaching Stummerberg is most practical by private car. From the Inntalautobahn A12, motorists exit at Wiesing onto the B169 Zillertalstraße and proceed to Stumm in the valley floor. From there, well-maintained, fully paved yet winding and steep mountain roads ascend to the hamlets between 800 and over 1,200 meters. During the winter months, appropriate winter tires and snow chains are essential equipment. Rail travelers take the scenic narrow-gauge Zillertalbahn to the Kaltenbach-Stumm station and transfer to local mountain taxis, seasonal hiking shuttles, or on-demand services to reach high-altitude guesthouses and trailheads.

Tipps

An exceptional nature excursion is a trek into the secluded Märzengrund. Beyond the rugged Märzenklamm gorge opens a pristine alpine valley; a gentle hike to the rustic Gmündalm at 1,196 meters leads through peaceful pine and spruce forests. This valley gained literary fame through dramatist Felix Mitterer's work depicting a local farmer's son who lived forty years as a solitary hermit in the Märzengrund. Keen mountaineers can ascend the 2,096-meter Hamberg, the local summit, starting from the Gasthof Almluft on the Gattererberg to enjoy magnificent vistas of the Zillertal and Kitzbühel Alps. Another highlight is the Alpengasthof Tannenalm at 1,040 meters, serving traditional Tyrolean cuisine while enjoying international renown as an alpine model glider airfield.
